critical_code_review_comments: RiskMeterPanel.tsx (line 154) defaults lineQ to 50 when sim_pctl_line_quantile_pct is missing — this would mis-classify edge cases as COIN FLIP. Acceptable today since the field is always returned alongside the p50 numeric guard, but worth documenting that the guard short-circuits before this default ever applies.

RiskMeterPanel.tsx writes `verdictFor(lineQ, isUnder)` — `lineQuantilePct` is defined as '% of samples ≤ threshold'. For Overs, winPct = 100 - lineQ is correct (we win when samples EXCEED the line). For Unders, winPct = lineQ is correct (we win when samples are ≤ line, except the strict-equality edge case is muddled when samples are integers and the line is .5 — current implementation handles it via the 'samples ≤ threshold' boundary which is fine for half-lines but ambiguous for whole-number lines). Half-lines are the norm in props so not a blocker.

sim_distribution.compute_percentiles uses NumPy 'linear' interpolation by hand — correct, but the docstring says 'NumPy's default linear method' and they should stay aligned if NumPy ever changes its default (NumPy 1.22 made 'linear' the default; safe through current versions).

Frontend pick/[id].tsx now safely guards both `pick.factors` and `pick.key_insights` — good. There are still other arrays referenced un-guarded later (`pick.top_reasons` at line 402 — checked via length>0 fallback to key_insights, so OK).
